verses.text: And King Astyages was gathered to his fathers, and Cyrus of Persia received his kingdome.
And Daniel conuersed with the king, and was honored above all his friends.
Now the Babylonians had an Idol called Bel, and there were spent on him every day twelue great measures of fine flowre, and fourtie sheepe, and six vessels of wine.
And the king worshipped it, and went daily to adore it: but Daniel worshipped his own Alahayam. And the king said to him, Why doest not you worship Bel?
Who answered and said, Because I may not worship idols made with hands, but the living Alahayam, who has created the heaven, and the earth, and has soueraigntie over all flesh.
Then saide the King to him, Thinkest you not that Bel is a living god? seest you not how much he eateth and drinketh every day?
Then Daniel smiled, and said, O king, be not deceiued: for this is but clay within, and brasse without, and did never eate or drinke any thing.
So the king was wroth, and called for his Priests, and said to them, If you tell me not who this is that deuoureth these expenses, you shall die.
But if you can certifie me that Bel deuoureth them, then Daniel shall die: for he has spoken blasphemie against Bel. And Daniel sayd to the king, Let it be according to your word.
(Now the Priests of Bel were threescore and tenne, beside their wiues and children) and the king went with Daniel into the temple of Bel.
So Bels Priests said, Loe, we goe out: but you, O king, set on the meate, and make ready the wine, and shut the doore fast, and seale it with your own signet:
And to morrow, when you commest in, if you findest not that Bel has eaten up all, we will suffer death; or else Daniel, that speaks falsely against us.
And they little regarded it: for under the table they had made a priuie entrance, whereby they entred in continually, and consumed those things.

So when they were gone forth, the king set meates before Bel. Now Daniel had commanded his servants to bring ashes, and those they strewed throughout all the temple, in the presence of the king alone: then went they out and shut the doore, & sealed it with the kings signet, and so departed.
Now in the night came the Priests with their wiues and children (as they were woont to do) and did eate and drinke up all.
In the morning betime the king arose, and Daniel with him.
And the king said, Daniel, are the seales whole? And he said, Yea, O king, they be whole.
And assoone as he had opened the doore, the king looked on the table, and cried with a loude voice, Great are you, O Bel, and with you is no deceit at all.
Then laughed Daniel, and helde the king that he should not goe in, and sayd, Behold now the pauement, and marke well whose footsteps are these.
And the king said, I see the footsteps of men, women and children: and then the king was angry,
And tooke the Priests, with their wiues and children, who showed him the priuy doores, where they came in, and consumed such things as were on the table.
Therefore the king slewe them, and deliuered Bel into Daniels power, who destroyed him and his temple.
And in that same place there was a great Dragon, which they of Babylon worshipped.
And the king said to Daniel, Will you also say that this is of brasse? loe, he liueth, he eateth and drinketh, you canst not say, that he is no living Alahayam: therefore worship him.
Then said Daniel to the king, I will worship the Lord my Alahayam: for he is the living Alahayam.
But give me leaue, O king, and I shall slay this dragon without sword or staffe. The king sayde, I give you leaue.

Then Daniel tooke pitch, fat, and haire, and did seethe them together, and made lumpes of it: this he put in the Dragons mouth, and so the Dragon burst in sunder: and Daniel said, Loe, these are the gods you worship.

When they of Babylon heard that, they tooke great indignation, and conspired against the king, saying, The king is become a Jew, and he has destroyed Bel, he has slaine the Dragon, and put the Priests to death.
So they came to the king, and said, Deliuer us Daniel, or else we will destroy you and your house.
Now when the king sawe that they pressed him sore, being constrained, he deliuered Daniel to them:
Who cast him into the lions den, where he was six days.
And in the den there were seven lyons, and they had given them every day two carkeises, and two sheepe: which then were not given to them, to the intent they might deuoure Daniel.
Now there was in Iury a Prophet called Habacuc, who had made pottage, & had broken bread in a boule, and was going into the field, for to bring it to the reapers.
But the Angel of the Lord said to Habacuc, Goe carrie the dinner that you have into Babylon to Daniel, who is in the lions denne.
And Habacuc said, Lord, I never saw Babylon: neither do I know where the denne is.
Then the Angel of the Lord tooke him by the crown, and bare him by the haire of his head, and through the vehemencie of his spirit, set him in Babylon over the den.
And Habacuc cryed, saying, O Daniel, Daniel, take the dinner which Alahayam has sent you.
And Daniel saide, You have remembred mee, O Alahayam: neither have you forsaken them that seeke you, and love you.
So Daniel arose and did eate: and the Angel of the Lord set Habacuc in his own place again immediatly.
Upon the seventh day the king went to bewaile Daniel: and when he came to the den, he looked in, and behold, Daniel was sitting.
Then cried the king with a loud voyce, saying, Great are you, O Lord Alahayam of Daniel, and there is none other besides you.
And he drew him out: and cast those that were the cause of his destruction into the den: and they were deuoured in a moment before his face.
